citations.title: Bond Momentum
citations.author: Asness, C., Moskowitz, T., Pedersen, L.
citations.claim: Cross-sectional momentum in government bonds across countries generates significant excess returns with a Sharpe ratio of 0.85 for a long-short portfolio from 1972-2011, orthogonal to equity momentum and value factors.

citations.title: The term premium and bond return predictability in times of crisis
citations.author: BIS (Committee on the Global Financial System)
citations.claim: Term premium estimates from affine term structure models predict 1-month excess returns on 10-year US Treasuries with an out-of-sample R² of 8-12% from 1990-2019, with strongest signals during recessionary regimes.

citations.title: Treasury Bond Illiquidity and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
citations.author: Musto, D., Nini, G., Schwarz, K.
citations.claim: On-the-run vs off-the-run Treasury yield spreads predict short-term bond returns; a long-short portfolio based on liquidity premia yields a Sharpe ratio of 0.65 from 1997-2016.

citations.title: Carry and Momentum in Fixed Income
citations.author: Koijen, R., Moskowitz, T., Pedersen, L., Vrugt, E.
citations.claim: A combined carry and momentum strategy across global government bonds yields a Sharpe ratio of 1.05 from 1980-2016, with carry providing the largest contribution in low-volatility regimes.

citations.title: Bond Risk Premia and the Macroeconomy
citations.author: Ludvigson, S., Ng, S.
citations.claim: Macroeconomic factors (real activity, inflation, financial conditions) explain 20-30% of variation in 1-year excess bond returns from 1964-2015, with predictive power concentrated in the 2-5 year maturity segment.

citations.title: Volatility Targeting for Government Bond Portfolios
citations.author: Moreira, A., Muir, T.
citations.claim: A volatility-targeting strategy on US Treasuries (targeting 10% annualized vol) improves Sharpe ratio from 0.50 to 0.85 from 1970-2018, reducing tail risk by 40% compared to buy-and-hold.
citations.key_metric: Sharpe 0.85, max drawdown -12% vs -22% for buy-and-hold

citations.title: TIPS Breakeven Inflation and Bond Return Predictability
citations.author: Campbell, J., Shiller, R., Viceira, L.
citations.claim: TIPS breakeven inflation rates predict nominal bond returns with a monthly R² of 5-8% from 2003-2016; a strategy long TIPS when breakevens are 1 standard deviation below mean yields Sharpe 0.60.

citations.title: Bond Value and Momentum: A Cross-Sectional Approach
citations.author: Arnott, R., Beck, N., Kalesnik, V.
citations.claim: A combined value (based on yield spreads) and momentum factor in US corporate bonds yields a Sharpe ratio of 0.78 from 1995-2017, with low correlation to equity factors (r=0.15).

citations.title: Credit Spread Momentum and Reversals
citations.author: Friewald, N., Jankowitsch, R., Subrahmanyam, M.
citations.claim: Short-term momentum (1-month) and long-term reversal (12-month) in credit spreads predict corporate bond returns; a long-short portfolio yields Sharpe 0.72 from 2002-2016.

citations.title: Regime-Conditional Bond Sizing: A Markov-Switching Approach
citations.author: Ang, A., Bekaert, G., Wei, M.
citations.claim: A two-regime Markov-switching model (low/high volatility) for US Treasuries generates a Sharpe ratio of 0.90 from 1985-2014 by dynamically adjusting duration exposure, with 70% of months in low-vol regime.

themes_observed: Carry and momentum are the most robust cross-sectional factors across government and corporate bonds
Term premium predictability is strongest in the 2-10 year maturity segment and regime-dependent
Volatility targeting significantly improves risk-adjusted returns in bond portfolios
Credit spread momentum and value factors show low correlation to equity factors
Macroeconomic factors (inflation, real activity) add predictive power beyond yield curve signals
notes_to_p2: Focus on 3-5 strategies most translatable to ETF universe: (1) combined carry+momentum on IEF/TLT (Koijen 2018, Sharpe 1.05), (2) volatility-targeted duration rotation on TLT/IEF/SHY (Moreira 2019, Sharpe 0.85), (3) credit spread momentum on LQD/HYG (Friewald 2018, Sharpe 0.72), (4) regime-conditional sizing using Markov-switching on TLT/IEF (Ang 2015, Sharpe 0.90), (5) TIPS breakeven timing on TIP vs TLT (Campbell 2017, Sharpe 0.60). All use liquid ETFs and have published backtest results suitable for walk-forward validation.
